anti_generic_signature_read: 'The cloche form: the lid is not a box lid, it's an observatory dome with a real slot cut through it, and the slot goes all the way from the crown down the flank.' Also named cold: the sun/moon pairing carried as relief rather than paint, the corner-post registration, and the inlaid square field 'rather than a printed or painted chequer'.
blind_action_read: 'Frame 1: closed... counters glint through the gap under the flange. Frame 2: the dome and flange have been lifted as one piece and float above the tray; the full board is revealed set up for play. Frame 3: the dome is gone entirely; only the loaded board remains. So: lid off, game out.'
blind_form_read: 'Four masses': a flat grey tray with a low rail and a square post proud at each corner; a pale chequer floor whose 32 slate-blue squares 'sit in shallow pockets, with a thin bright land between them'; a thin square teal lid flange; and a hemisphere on a stepped collar - 'a taller cylindrical skirt plus a thin proud rim below it' - about 70% of the plate's width. It read the dome as dominating and the game beneath as a plinth.
blind_held_read: Unprompted, before knowing anything: 'A two-hands-sized boxed draughts set: a shallow grey tray with a blue-and-white 8x8 chequer floor holding 24 round counters, closed by a big teal hemisphere on a square flange that drops over the whole tray like a cloche. Lid off, it is a checkers board; lid on, it is a paperweight-ish model of a domed observatory.' It reached 'draughts set', 'observatory' and 'the lid lifts off' with no prompting of any kind.
blind_relationship_read: 'Flange carries dome; flange lands on the tray rail; the four corner posts sit outboard of the flange and nominally locate it.' 'The tube is fused to the dome's inner floor. It is therefore part of the lid, not of the base.' 'Lift-flange -> dome, tube and slot all leave together -> board is exposed.' In round 6 it withdrew its reading of the flange as perched, against the measured 0.8 mm per-side spigot into the 184.0 mm opening and the four integral corner ledges at z21.0.
blind_subjects_read: 24 counters, 12 orange-terracotta and 12 pale cream; the orange face 'a plain centre circle ringed by eight small marks', which it read cold as 'closer to a bearing race, a gear hub or a camera-aperture icon than a sun'; the cream face 'a single hairline crescent outline... sits well left of the disc centre'; kings as two counters stacked; and 'a tube in a slot: a plain dark cylinder with a square-cut muzzle showing a clean annular wall'. The gear-hub reading is the product's own disclosed divergence, found cold, and the critic recorded that it does not break the subject match.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind, on roof/slit-elevation_az-90_el0.png: 'a straight-sided channel is cut down through the middle of the dome, AND IT TAKES THE CROWN WITH IT: the dome's profile rises on the left to a peak, stops, and instead of carrying over the top it is interrupted by two flat parallel walls and the flat floor between them, then resumes on the right.' It first read the plan frame as showing a slot that 'does not reach the zenith', called that its one tradeable finding, and withdrew it without reservation against the measurement: 0.000000 mm3 of roof in a 4 mm column on the dome's own axis between z85.5 and the apex, where the dome would be solid to r 10.2 mm at z89.0.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The slit runs the full height of the dome - from its far edge, over the apex, down the near flank - and stops at the springing line, the drum top, instead of being cut down to the plate.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind, from four azimuths 90 degrees apart, by a critic who did not know to look for a ring: 'No. The band is continuous through 360 degrees... an unbroken two-step collar... with no notch, no joint, no rebate, no keyway and no door. Specifically at az-90, where the slot faces the camera, the slot's two parallel walls run down and simply die on the top edge of the collar; the collar's dark upper line passes straight across in front of them without interruption.' Measured: 0.000000 mm3 of gap at z 4.0, 7.0, 9.0, 10.7, 13.0 and 14.0.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Below the slit the drum is whole and its rotation ring runs unbroken all the way round.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind: 'The tube simply widens at the bottom into a smooth conical flare that dissolves into the flat floor of the slot.' Round 5, on the axial elevation: 'Standing in that channel is a tube. It rises from the floor near the collar... At the bottom the tube spreads into a smooth cove that flows out into the floor of the channel on both sides, with no line where it lands.' Measured: the material standing in the slit is one body whose lowest point is z14.700000, the floor plane itself.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The telescope stands on the floor of the slit, on its own footing, as its own pier.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 5, on roof/foot-macro_az-90_el55.png: 'The cove is a clean, even, circular collar all the way round the tube - the generous cove carried right round the foot is exactly what is there, and from this angle it is obvious and well-formed.' Built radius 6.0 mm; root 26.4246 mm across the slit by 35.246 mm along it, 1.7877 mm clear of each slit wall.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Where the tube meets that floor it is blended with a generous cove fillet carried right round the foot, so the root spreads into the floor instead of meeting it at a line.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind, unprompted: the stub is 'about 4% of the dome's width'. Round 4: 'It clears, and 4% of diameter is as close to only just as you will get.' Measured: 2.5855 mm on the axis and 3.8993 mm to the farthest material, 0.26 of the tube's own diameter, inside the brief's 2.5-7.0 mm window on both readings.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The muzzle clears the shell, and only just.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 5, on roof/slit-elevation_az-90_el0.png: the tube 'runs up to just below the shoulder line', which the critic recorded as settling this directly rather than by the positional inference it had used in round 4. Measured: muzzle top z84.8645, nominal apex z89.7, built high point z88.1847.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The muzzle stays below the top of the dome.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind, unprompted figure: 'essentially all of it is inside... Call it 85-90% swallowed, 10-15% showing.' Round 5: 'its length filling about half the dome's width - as long as the dome's radius.' Measured: 82.69 mm of the 85.3 mm lies inside the dome.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Most of the tube's length is inside the dome, visible down the open slit.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind: 'a plain dark cylinder with a square-cut muzzle showing a clean annular wall'. Round 5: 'The top is an open mouth, a clean bright annulus with a dark bore inside it.' Built: 7.0 mm bore 13.0 mm deep in a 15.0 mm tube, leaving a 4.0 mm wall.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The muzzle stays open, with a visible wall thickness round it.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 5, cold on the axial elevation before deciding anything: 'an open, opened-up dome with a long vertical pipe standing inside it, mouth pointing at the sky... a periscope, a flue, a telescope aimed at the zenith. It does not read as a barrel poking through a wall, because you can see its whole length and you can see it standing on a floor. It reads as a thing inside a building.' Scored NOT MATCHED in round 4 when judged in the one elevation where the shutter is edge-on, and MATCHED in round 5 when judged in the frames the requirement's own text names.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The result reads as a long instrument standing on the observatory floor and lying across an open dome, most of its length visible down the open slit, only its mouth clearing the shell - not a short barrel poking through a wall.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind, with no options offered and no knowledge of the requirement: 'First three words: snapped-off peg. Runners-up: broken tab, sawn stub.' Second guesses, unprompted: 'a lifting nub or a lug for a strap', 'a vent or chimney'. Round 4, on being told the four forbidden readings: 'Plainly: none of spout, cannon, mortar or gun is among my readings. Not one of the four.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE. In the straight side elevation, camera level with the dome, the thing sticking out must NOT read as a spout, a cannon, a mortar or a gun.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 3, blind: 'There is no fork, no yoke, no pier, no trunnion, no pivot pin, no bearing block, no ring, no strap, no clamp, no base plate, no fork-arms either side.' Measured: exactly one lump of material inside the slit at z 15.2, 18.0, 25.0, 40.0, 60.0 and 78.0, each centred on x=0 within 0.000001 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE. No fork, no two arms, no keel, no pier and no rectangular foot block. Above the floor the ONLY thing standing in the slit is the telescope itself.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4, against its round-3 frames: nothing outboard was seen anywhere but the muzzle, and the four drum frames show the collar's outline as a clean uninterrupted curve in every direction. Measured: 0.000000 mm3 of roof outside the 75.0 mm drum radius between the plate top at z3.0 and the springing line at z14.7.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE. Nothing projects outboard of the dome or the drum at any height, other than the muzzle.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'none of my raw readings is the foot block... The previous critic's named object is gone.' Round 5, on the root from above: the cove is 'a clean, even, circular collar all the way round the tube... obvious and well-formed'. The remaining stock readings it listed - flat crosscut muzzle, constant-diameter shaft, square-cut slit walls - are the frozen tube and slit specification, which it labelled as out of scope itself.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE. Nothing in the slit reads as the raw, sawn-off, untreated foot block the previous critic named: the stock-looking bracket is gone and nothing has replaced it.

largest_risk: Nothing has ever been printed, and the most fragile thing on the object is the newest: a 15 mm free-standing tube whose only attachment is a 6.0 mm cove fillet on the floor of a 30 mm slot, cantilevered 85.3 mm with its centre of mass 17.6 mm outside its foot, required to print support-free at 45 degrees. The critic's words: the telescope is the part most likely to arrive snapped, drooping or fused to the slot wall. No physical test backs the fillet and the product makes no print-ready claim.
resolution: Four rounds, one critic, transcripts in cad/review/revision-d/ rounds 3-6. Round 3 fully blind: 43 images, nothing else on disk, no options offered. Unprompted it said 'draughts set', 'observatory', 'lid off, game out' and read the sun mark as a gear hub, which is this product's own disclosed divergence. All four questions section F required were put in that blind round. Round 4 revealed the brief and scored 11/13 with two blocking defects; round 5 resolved both - the zenith one against a measurement the critic itself had asked for, and the instrument-reading one after I corrected a framing error of mine, giving it a requirement with no frames attached. Round 6 returned NO on finished-and-desirable and held it through one re-wording; it was withdrawn only against two measurements, the 0.75 mm of dark inlay showing round every counter and the 0.8 mm per-side spigot seat, both of which the critic accepted without independently verifying and said so. Final: 13/13 matched, blocking list empty, nine of nine judgements yes. Two earlier rounds by a FIRST critic are preserved as history in the same directory; they read superseded frames and superseded geometry and are not evidence for anything here. Two framing errors of mine are recorded in GEOMETRY-NOTES.md D9b, D9d and D9e rather than argued away. The critic's standing objection, unscored: the aperture dies on an unbroken rotation ring and it believes viewers read it as an aperture that cannot open - the commissioner chose that trade knowingly.
reviewer: One independent native critic, blind to the Wish, the brief and the product identity for the whole of round 3 and told to read nothing but the 43 images. Rounds 4-6 primed. See cad/review/revision-d/.
